nodes.description: Overall seawater splitting in AEM electrolyzer
nodes.source_text: S doping improved activity (HER overpotential: 25 mV; OER overpotential: 243 mV), long-term durability (1000 h at 100 mA cm⁻²), and near 100% Faradaic efficiency (FE). The S-RuO₂-based anion exchange membrane seawater electrolyzer required only 2.01 V to reach 1.0 A cm⁻².
Finally, Mo-doped γ-MnO₂ demonstrated excellent OER performance with a low overpotential of 0.27 V while effectively suppressing ClOR, exhibiting high selectivity.

nodes.description: OER stability in alkaline seawater electrolyzer
nodes.source_text: The optimally phosphate-intercalated NiFe LDH anode demonstrated stable operation for over 1000 h at a high current density of 1.0 A cm⁻² in a 2 W-scale alkaline seawater electrolyzer (ASWE).

nodes.description: OER stability in simulated alkaline seawater
nodes.source_text: Experimental results showed that NiFe LDH_CO₃²⁻ exhibits excellent stability under simulated alkaline seawater conditions at current densities of 500 and 1000 mA cm⁻². Furthermore, a two-electrode system maintained high stability over 400 h within a current density range of 100-1000 mA cm⁻² in alkaline seawater.
Consequently, this catalyst demonstrated a degradation rate of 20 μV h⁻¹ during long-term operation at 100 mA cm⁻² (>1500 h).

nodes.description: OER stability in high Cl⁻ electrolyte
nodes.source_text: As shown in Figure 6j, in electrolytes with high Cl⁻ concentration, the current of NiCoP@NF rapidly drops within 5 h, whereas NiCoP_v@NF maintains relatively stable performance for at least 20 h.

nodes.description: OER and corrosion resistance in natural seawater
nodes.source_text: Theoretical and experimental results indicated that the adsorption energies of OH⁻ and Cl⁻ on CeO₂/D-NiFe-LDH are -0.61, -0.72 eV and -0.35, -0.21 eV, respectively, demonstrating that CeO₂/D-NiFe-LDH exhibits superior OER activity in seawater compared to NiFeAl₀-LDH. CeO₂/D-NiFe-LDH also showed lower corrosion current and corrosion potential.

nodes.description: OER and CER evaluation in artificial seawater
nodes.source_text: Compared with CoO/CC, MoO₃@CoO/CC showed negligible CER in artificial seawater, confirming that the MoO₃ layer effectively shields Cl⁻ and enables selective catalysis. Cl⁻ detector measurements after 50 h of OER showed that the Cl⁻ concentration remains almost unchanged.
